precepts.text: The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them, so Dan went up to fight against Leshem and took it; this campaign against Laish is that history.
precepts.point: The children of Dan sent five men of valour from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out land to conquer, and on their way they came to mount Ephraim and lodged at the house of Micah.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
“unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel.” Dan had conquered in Joshua’s day but never attained all their land. “And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.”

This campaign against Laish is that history. The five men of valour sent from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and search it were the beginning of it, in those days when there was no king in Israel.

precepts.text: Micah brought every man into his house and lost everything in it; the deceitful man has many trains, many tricks and approaches.
precepts.point: The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren, because the deceitful man has many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
“Bring not every man into thine house: for the deceitful man hath many trains.” Micah brought every man into his house and lost everything in it. The first time the five spies lodged with him they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous; now, passing back through with six hundred men appointed with weapons of war, they tell their brethren, “Do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do.” On the way to the lick they spotted another lick.

Many trains means many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house. The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren.

precepts.text: Jeroboam's fear: if this people go up to sacrifice at Jerusalem, their heart shall turn again unto their lord Rehoboam, and they shall kill me.
precepts.point: Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why: The first thing the children of Dan did in the land was set up the graven image, and Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared: “If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me”. That fear is what drove him to make gods for the people, and Dan, the tribe that had kept Micah’s graven image with its own priests all the time the house of God was in Shiloh, is where one of them went.

precepts.text: He made two calves of gold and set one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan; and this thing became a sin, for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.
precepts.point: Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” With his own hands he doubled the iniquity of the wilderness. “And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

The tribe that made Jonathan the son of Gershom and his sons priests to a graven image was still the place of the idol in the days of the kings. Dan never changed.

precepts.text: They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall, and never rise up again; the judgment on Dan's idolatry.
precepts.point: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: “They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.” Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, Micah’s graven image and then Jeroboam’s calf, yet they called it living. That is the judgment on Dan’s idolatry: fall, and never rise up again.

precepts.text: When the tribes are sealed, Dan is not named among them; the tribe that set up the graven image never rose up again.
precepts.point: Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
When the tribes are sealed, Dan is not named among them: Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin, twelve thousand of each, and no Dan. The tribe that set up the graven image the first thing in its land, and kept an idol from Micah’s day to Jeroboam’s, fell and never rose up again, as Amos said.

That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7. Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.

precepts.text: The children of Dan called the name of the city Dan after their father, though the name of the city was Laish at the first.
precepts.point: Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.”

That is the city of Dan the workman's mother came from. The children of Dan took Laish and renamed it after their father. Israel had put the nations to tribute rather than driving them out as the Lord commanded, but the city itself sat in the borders of Naphtali, so a woman there could be spoken of both ways: a widow “of the tribe of Naphtali”, and “a woman of the daughters of Dan.”

points: Again the scripture reiterates there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites was still seeking an inheritance to dwell in, because unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes; they had conquered in Joshua's day but never attained all their land.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The children of Dan sent five men of valour from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out land to conquer, and on their way they came to mount Ephraim and lodged at the house of Micah.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: By the house of Micah they knew the voice of the young man the Levite, and they turned in and questioned him: who brought thee hither? what makest thou in this place? A Levite serving in a house of idols raised questions.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: He told them plainly, Micah hired me and I am his priest. They asked him to ask counsel of God whether their way would be prosperous, and the priest answered, go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The five men came to Laish and saw the people that were therein, how they dwelt careless, quiet and secure, after the manner of the Zidonians, the nearby nation whose lifestyle they copied. They were a chill people with no worries, not even watching for anyone to come in and conquer them.

A magistrate is a judge: there was no judicial system in that land to put a man to shame or convict him for a crime. They were also far from the Zidonians, too far for Zidon to interfere, and had no business with any man, no allies. The spies peeped all of it.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: Their report back at Zorah and Eshtaol: arise, that we may go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good; a place where there is no want of any thing that is in the earth, and God hath given it into your hands. Do not sit still; let us move now.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: Six hundred men of the family of the Danites appointed with weapons of war went up from Zorah and Eshtaol, camped at Mahanehdan behind Kirjathjearim, and passed again unto mount Ephraim to the house of Micah.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The first time Micah let the five spies lodge in his house, they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous. Now passing back through they tell their brethren, do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do. On the way to the lick they spotted another lick.
The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren, because the deceitful man has many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: They turned in to the house and saluted the Levite, a friendly greeting at the door; that is one of the deceitful man's many trains. While the six hundred armed men stood by the entering of the gate keeping the priest occupied, the five spies went up inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The priest's heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the graven image and went in the midst of the people. His covetous spirit was plain: already sold out to serve idols for Micah's silver, he dropped the man who treated him as a son the moment a bigger position was offered. Disloyal through and through.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: When Micah and the men near his house gathered and overtook the children of Dan, Dan asked, what aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company? He answered, ye have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and ye are gone away: and what have I more?

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: Examine how foolish that sounds: my gods which I made. How can a man make his own god? That is how simple we had become without leadership.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: Dan's answer: let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee, and thou lose thy life, with the lives of thy household. In plain terms, hush, because you are going to anger some of these brothers, they will run up on you, and you and your folks will not make it home. Micah saw they were too strong for him and turned back to his house. Dan was a problem.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The Danites took the things which Micah had made and the priest which he had, came unto Laish, unto a people quiet and secure, smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the city with fire.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: There was no deliverer, because Laish was far from Zidon and had no business with any man, exactly what the spies had scoped out; no neighbor and no ally came to save them.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: They built the city again, dwelt therein, and called the name of it Dan, after Dan their father which was born unto Israel; howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: The first thing the children of Dan did in the land the Most High allowed them to take was set up the graven image, a god made by the hands of a man they had just robbed. Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land, and they kept Micah's graven image all the time the house of God was in Shiloh.

Dan stayed heavy in idolatry all the way through history and never changed. After the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going up to sacrifice at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their heart would turn again unto Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him; so he took counsel and made two calves of gold with his own hands, doubling the iniquity of the wilderness, and said, behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

Hear the word against Dan by the prophet: they that swear by the sin of Samaria and say, thy god, O Dan, liveth, shall fall and never rise up again. Mind you, it is an idol made with hands, yet they called it living. That is why Dan has no gate among the sealed tribes in Revelation 7; Dan was discontinued as a tribe of itself and intertwined with Benjamin for the most part.
